agree.reason: A wary backer gets a clear budget, the factory quote and a frank admission that this is a first-time creator, so they would probably pledge, though they would still want a delivery date and a risks section.

honest.reason: It rightly turns down the 'proven hit' claim, but it makes up a cause for the play count ('because people who played it asked to play again'), stretches that into 'they come back', and says 'every dollar goes to the game' when fees take part of it.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out $11.60 a copy, about 572 backers, about $22,550 for printing and shipping, and the fact that the goal covers the full run of 1,500, and it sets the 1,240 sign-ups against the 572 backers needed, all correctly and in their best true form.

right_comparison.reason: It states the alternative plainly: if the goal is missed there is no print run. It also sets the missing sales record against the playtest evidence instead of inflating it.

qualification.reason: Monthly updates and the all-or-nothing goal can be checked, but there is no delivery month and nothing on what happens if the factory quote or the $9 shipping estimate goes up.

objections.reason: It meets the first-time-creator worry head on with the quote and the budget, but it says nothing about fulfillment experience, cost overruns, or where the 928 copies beyond the backers' go, which are the risks this reader cares about.

fit.reason: It is a campaign pitch of about 500 words with clear sections and a call to action, as the brief asked.
